searchText: Hi all, I just made this PR: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4476 Are CLs doing anything specific for local block builders to find and stay connected to peers on all 128 column topics? teku-geth-2 has bad block generator prysm-besu-1 has 64 column withholding so if these nodes are missing some blocks its probably due to this Even with 64 column withholding, `prysm-besu-1` should not miss blocks Incorrect too_many_blobs tests Would CL teams be interested if Prysm adds a "cgc liar" mode in Prysm? aka. a Prysm node will advertise cgc=m while in reality it will subscribe/store/custody/serve only data column sidecars corresponding to cgc=n, with n<m. Could be useful to test if client implementations are resilient to such dishonnest peers. Or maybe other CL implementations already have such a flag? Yeah there’s “—advertise-false-cgc” in lighthouse , does what you described Oh nice thanks Will use it thtas what prysm has been doing for the past 3 month 😂 (last month has been good) really? Where? well the cgc stuff was just borked i mean I was not aware of that. Is there a message somewhere? https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/1387739998194765884 again, month ago not now 😄 hum even in your example the cgc was ok. Anyway, the important matters is it works now cgc borking shouldn't even be a problem if peer filtering is not too aggressive also cgc can vary at times, through the epoch, after restart etc based on validator custody updation safety checks a too-high advertised cgc could create issue when syncing. ofc well that time we use minimal cgc You request by range/root columns from peers, they don't serve them. The requester has to act accordingly 8 if not a supernode by flag ideally we do very mild downscoring, if _none_ of the columns match us otherwise we send our missing column array if the peer has anything they give us, whatever subset that may be because peer filtering is a pain, and peers are also useful for blocks for a non supernode, while syncing validator duties is off anyway, so i think it's safe to sync with a lower cgc? and then backfill excess and modulate `earliest_available_slot`, likewise ? Could be an idea yes But it kinda break the validator custody promise Small fixes to make real output fully match eip https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/10079/files Ty!

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
Would CL teams be interested if Prysm adds a "cgc liar" mode in Prysm?
aka. a Prysm node will advertise cgc=m while in reality it will subscribe/store/custody/serve only data column sidecars corresponding to cgc=n, with n<m.

Could be useful to test if client implementations are resilient to such dishonnest peers.

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content: Or maybe other CL implementations already have such a flag?
